rtl_snippet: always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrst_n) begin

fix.rationale:
Tracing the cell sequence against the two attributed endpoints shows the path is: cycle_counter bit (uart_rx.v:170, register _124902_) -> next_bit / n_fsm_state / uart_rx_valid logic in uart_rx.v (cells 1-6: NOR4, NAND4, OAI22, NOR2, AOI211, AND3 - almost certainly the wide COUNT_REG_LEN-bit (~14-bit, since CYCLES_PER_BIT=50MHz/9600baud≈5208) equality comparator plus the FSM case/ternary mux) -> fifo2_winc gating in uart_wrapper.v (cell 7, AND3) -> wbinnext increment, wgraynext gray-encode and wfull_val compare in wptr_full.v (cells 8-12: NAND3 carry, XOR2 gray bit, XOR2 gray bit, XOR2 compare, NOR3 reduce) -> wfull/awfull register at wptr_full.v:52 (endpoint).

Only the last ~0.34 ns (cells 8-12) of the 0.94 ns summed chain, and only the last register, fall inside the RTL I'm allowed to edit (wptr_full.v). The larger contributors (cells 1-7, ~0.52 ns, the wide cycle-counter comparator and FSM next-state mux) live in uart_rx.v, which is explicitly read-only context here.

Within wptr_full.v itself:
- RETIME is not available: wbin/wptr update in one always block and awfull/wfull update in a second always block on the same clock edge, but wfull_val is computed combinationally from the *current* wbin (via wbinnext/wgraynext) in the same cycle - there is no register sitting inside this combinational chain to slide. wbin and wfull are already exactly one register hop apart with nothing in between to move.
- RESTRUCTURE is not safely available: the code already implements the minimal-depth "simplified full-test" comparator (the commented-out three-term AND-of-compares form is the naive version; the single-compare form actually used is already the optimized rewrite). The wbinnext adder is a plain +1 increment on a 5-bit counter (ADDRSIZE=4); its carry chain is already about as shallow as a ripple increment gets for this width, and per the cost table, replacing narrow carry gates (NAND3/AND3) with wider lookahead gates is not guaranteed to be faster and can be slower - I have no synthesis feedback to prove a net win, so I can't certify equivalence-preserving improvement.
- PIPELINE is unsafe here: wfull is fed back into its own next-state computation (`winc & ~wfull` inside wbinnext) and also drives fifo2_winc/backpressure logic in uart_wrapper.v and the async_fifo write-side handshake, all outside this module's visibility. Delaying wfull/awfull by even one cycle would change when writes are blocked/accepted and would require re-balancing consumer logic I cannot see or verify from this scope.

A correct fix would most plausibly retime or pipeline the wide cycle_counter/next_bit comparator inside uart_rx.v (rtl/vendor/uart/rtl/uart_rx.v, around the `next_bit`/`p_n_fsm_state` logic feeding lines ~108-123), which is outside the RTL I was given permission to modify. Given the negative slack is small (-0.02 ns) but the dominant delay is off-scope and the in-scope tail offers no provably safe reduction, I report NO_FIX for this module.
